peace.human_summary: The natural full-service crossing when your trip already runs through Buffalo and Fort Erie, especially for commercial traffic or travelers who need pedestrian or bicycle access.
best_for: Travelers who should not make a large northbound detour for a small wait difference
peace.approach_character: U.S. traffic approaches from the Buffalo I-190 corridor; the Canadian side connects into Fort Erie and the QEW corridor.
peace.on_the_ground: This is the southern Niagara River crossing. Moving from Peace Bridge to the Falls-area bridges is a meaningful route change, so a small customs-wait advantage elsewhere is not enough to justify switching.
peace.watch_for: Passenger, commercial and trusted-traveler lanes can report different conditions. Pedestrians and bicycles use published inspection routing rather than vehicle lanes.

rainbow.human_summary: The most natural bridge for many Niagara Falls visitor trips because it connects the Niagara Falls districts on both sides and accepts general passenger, bus, trailer, pedestrian and bicycle traffic.
best_for: Travelers whose route already centers on the Falls district
rainbow.approach_character: The U.S. approach feeds from I-190 into Niagara Falls; the Canadian side connects toward Highway 420 and the QEW.
rainbow.on_the_ground: Rainbow and Whirlpool are geographically close, but they serve very different travelers: Rainbow is the general Falls crossing, while Whirlpool is a trusted-traveler specialist crossing.
rainbow.watch_for: Commercial trucks are not permitted. A short posted wait at another bridge still has to overcome the route-switch guardrail before the tool recommends leaving the Falls corridor.

whirlpool.human_summary: A specialized Niagara Falls crossing for NEXUS autos, with Global Entry accepted U.S.-bound only. It is not a general-purpose alternate bridge.
best_for: Global Entry travelers entering the U.S. only
Trips already positioned for the Whirlpool corridor
whirlpool.approach_character: The bridge sits in the Niagara Falls urban corridor between Rainbow and Lewiston–Queenston and operates on a more limited schedule than the other vehicle bridges.
whirlpool.on_the_ground: Whirlpool can look attractive on a map because it is close to Rainbow, but eligibility is the first question. Its operator wait is hourly context rather than equivalent real-time evidence, so the engine will not use it to justify a switch.
whirlpool.watch_for: NEXUS is required Canada-bound. No commercial trucks, pedestrians, bicycles or anything in tow. Published hours are 7:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.

lewiston-queenston.human_summary: The northern Niagara option for passenger and commercial traffic, particularly trips naturally running through Lewiston, Queenston, Niagara-on-the-Lake or Highway 405.
lewiston-queenston.approach_character: The U.S. side connects through I-190 and the Lewiston corridor; the Canadian side uses Highway 405 toward the QEW and Queenston.
lewiston-queenston.on_the_ground: This crossing is materially north of Rainbow and Whirlpool. It can be an excellent alternate when waits are very different, but a modest border-wait advantage can disappear in the extra drive.
lewiston-queenston.watch_for: Pedestrians are not permitted. NEXUS lane availability has published time windows rather than continuous dedicated service in both directions.
